title: Canonical presentation of an ind-constructible sheaf
statement:
Use the universe and small-site convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and a separated scheme $X$ of finite type over $k$, as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and a finite intermediate extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $\Lambda=\underline E$ or $\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}$ be the condensed coefficient ring of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], and let $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ as in [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Work in $\mathcal M=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_X}$, the category of internal module objects of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Write $\mathcal C=\operatorname{Cons}(X,\Lambda)$ for its full subcategory of constructible sheaves [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and $\operatorname{IndCons}(X,\Lambda)$ for the full replete subcategory of objects isomorphic to small filtered colimits of objects of $\mathcal C$, as in [det-ind-heart-full-faithfulness]. Filtered diagrams and colimits have the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

Let $B\in\operatorname{IndCons}(X,\Lambda)$. Let $J(B)$ have objects $(C,c)$ with $C\in\mathcal C$ and $c:C\to B$, and morphisms $f:(C,c)\to(C',c')$ the maps $f:C\to C'$ satisfying $c'f=c$. Then $J(B)$ is essentially small and filtered, and its tautological cocone with legs $c:C\to B$ is a colimit in $\mathcal M$:
$$B\simeq\varinjlim_{(C,c)\in J(B)}C.$$
Here a colimit over an essentially small category is taken over a small skeleton. For every small filtered presentation $B\simeq\varinjlim_{i\in I}C_i$ with each $C_i\in\mathcal C$, the functor $F:I\to J(B)$ induced by the presentation cocone is final (cofinal).

proof.text: First verify the hypotheses of the cited sheaf results. A field is Noetherian, since its only ideals are zero and itself, and its spectrum consists of one point, hence is quasi-compact. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$: $X$ is Noetherian. Thus the standing-scheme hypothesis in [sk-lem-coefficient-heart] and the Noetherian hypothesis in [det-ind-heart-full-faithfulness] hold with precisely the condensed coefficients and internal-module category in the statement. For essential smallness, part (2) of [sk-lem-coefficient-heart] gives a set of representatives $C$ of constructible objects. By [def-weil-size-convention] the site is small in the enlarged universe. A sheaf map is a family of section maps satisfying equations, hence its collection is a set in that universe. For each representative $C$, the maps $C\to B$ therefore form a set. Their union gives a set of representatives of $J(B)$; its Hom sets are subsets of sheaf Hom sets. This proves essential smallness. For each constructible $C$ choose an isomorphism $u:C\to C_0$ to its representative; $(C,c)$ is isomorphic over $B$ to $(C_0,c u^{-1})$. Restriction of cocones to these representatives and extension along these isomorphisms are inverse, so all colimit arguments may use the resulting small full subcategory.

source.place: First paragraph; standing hypotheses verified using Stacks 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian)

proof.text: The zero sheaf is constructible: take the zero finitely presented scalar module in the local-model definition [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Hence $(0,0\to B)$ makes $J(B)$ nonempty. Given $(C_1,c_1)$ and $(C_2,c_2)$, the split exact sequence $0\to C_1\to C_1\oplus C_2\to C_2\to0$ and extension closure in [sk-lem-coefficient-heart](1) show that $C_1\oplus C_2$ is constructible; the map with components $c_1,c_2$ gives a common successor in $J(B)$. For parallel $g,h:(C_1,c_1)\rightrightarrows(C_2,c_2)$, one has $c_2(g-h)=0$. The cokernel universal property gives a factorization of $c_2$ through $q:C_2\to\operatorname{coker}(g-h)$. The cokernel is constructible by the same closure clause, and $qg=qh$. Thus this quotient is an equalizing successor in $J(B)$, proving filteredness.

Part (2) of [det-ind-heart-full-faithfulness] gives a small filtered constructible diagram with colimit isomorphic to $B$; compose its cocone legs with that isomorphism to get a presentation cocone with vertex $B$. Now fix any such presentation, indexed by $I$, with legs $c_i:C_i\to B$, and let $F(i)=(C_i,c_i)$. For this presentation, enlarge the small full subcategory of step 1 by all the objects $F(i)$. Since $I$ is small this subcategory remains small and still meets every isomorphism class of $J(B)$, and $F$ now lands in it. Apply the criterion and the colimit comparison below to this small subcategory; extension of cocones as in step 1 recovers the colimit over $J(B)$. The objectwise argument below also applies to every object of the original $J(B)$ and proves finality there. For $j=(C,c)\in J(B)$, part (1) of that same node identifies $\varinjlim_i\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(C,C_i)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(C,B)$. Surjectivity gives $s:C\to C_i$ with $c_i s=c$, so $j\to F(i)$ exists. For two maps $s,s':j\to F(i)$ their images coincide in that Hom colimit. The elementary set-colimit calculation is as follows: take the disjoint union of the Hom sets modulo the transition relations. Equality is a finite zigzag of those relations. Filteredness supplies a cocone on its finite index diagram (combine the finitely many objects, then equalize the finitely many resulting parallel arrows), so the representatives agree after maps to a common stage. If those two maps out of $i$ differ, equalize them once more. Thus a single $t:i\to i'$ satisfies $C(t)s=C(t)s'$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-initial-functor-cofiltered-criterion](1) to $\mathcal A=I^{\mathrm{op}}$, $\mathcal B=J(B)^{\mathrm{op}}$, and $H=F^{\mathrm{op}}$: the two conditions just proved become exactly its conditions (i) and (ii). Hence $H$ is initial and $F$ is final. This establishes cofinality for every presentation, not only the chosen one.

source.place: Cofinality paragraph; Stacks 04E6 (definition-cofinal), via the existing dual criterion

proof.text: Let $G:J(B)\to\mathcal M$ be the tautological functor $(C,c)\mapsto C$. Use the colimit-existence and comparison clause of [lem-weil-pbc-initial-functor-cofiltered-criterion](1) with $H=F^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $M=G$. It says that the colimit of $G$ exists if and only if the colimit of $GF$ exists, and that its canonical comparison is an isomorphism. The latter colimit exists and is $B$ by the presentation in step 3. In particular the comparison $a:B\to\varinjlim G$ satisfies $a c_i=\iota_{F(i)}$. The cocone with legs $c:C\to B$ induces $b:\varinjlim G\to B$ by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and $ba c_i=c_i$ for all $i$. The colimit uniqueness for the presentation yields $ba=1_B$, so $b=a^{-1}$. Consequently $B$, with precisely its tautological legs $c$, is the claimed colimit. No existence of the colimit over $J(B)$ was assumed.

split_report.summary: Repair of return for changed det-ind-heart-full-faithfulness statement: reread current hypotheses and both clauses, exposed the source's standing scheme and condensed-module conventions, verified Noetherianity, and replaced stale quotation text. Reused the existing cofiltered initial-functor Mathlib leaf by taking opposites, eliminating the duplicate proposed final-functor leaf and proving colimit existence before comparison. Expanded the elementary eventual-equality argument for general filtered categories and checked the tautological cocone legs.
split_report.blueprint: The four steps realize the first essential-smallness paragraph, the *Filtered* paragraph, the *Cofinality* paragraph, and the *Colimit* paragraph of sk-prop-ind-heart-canonical-presentation.proof.md.

tool_uses.why: Generic initial/final-functor criterion and existence/comparison of ordinary colimits, specialized to F.op; the unit supplies the finite-presentation argument but no such general category-theory theorem.

The small subcategory is enlarged by the F(i) so that it stays small and full.
